newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters says no employer contributions to NZ super.
newsitem.headline: Peters says no employer contributions to NZ super.

text.p: Employer contributions would not be part of the compulsory retirement savings scheme put to a referendum in September, Treasurer Winston Peters said on Thursday.
Asked after a speech to a retirement summit if the team designing the proposed scheme had considered employer contributions, Peters said: "They may have, but it will not be a feature."
In his speech Peters outlined how sustainability would be his key battleground in arguing for the scheme.
"The real issues become, which scheme is affordable and sustainable during the lives of today's working generation?"
He said critics who had argued the current universal pension scheme was sustainable talked about increasing the age of entitlement, increased immigration or taxes or decreased entitlements.

"What we have endeavoured to do is take every feature of New Zealand Superannuation into the new retirement savings regime. So the aged entitlements and the financial entitlements remain the same for everybody as at July 1 next year," Peters said.
He said there needed to be a distinction drawn between savings schemes, where people could take out money and spend it, and retirement schemes.

"Those who are able to take money out, spend it on travel, boats, cars, blow their contributions in whatever way they like, do not have a superannuation retirement scheme. They have a savings scheme."
Peters had earlier indicated savers would be required to take out an annuity under the proposed scheme.
